transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Clara (Redwood SE), Joanne Rios (CISO, Penumbra), Martin Adler (Head of Cloud Ops), Lina Gomez (Legal), Evan Murthy (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated sections:
- Topics: Data residency / region pinning, KMS custody and escrow, subprocessor list, audit logs, SSO/RBAC implications
- Action items: listed below

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, account exec for Penumbra. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Joanne: Joanne here, CISO at Penumbra. Martin and Lina are on too.
[00:09] Martin: Martin, hi.
[00:11] Lina: Lina from legal.
[00:13] Evan: Evan, platform eng, hi.
[00:15] Clara: Clara, solutions engineer at Redwood. We'll take you through the region and security controls.

[02:05] Samir: Goal for today is to confirm how we can enforce EU-only processing for EU customer data, understand K M S custody options, and get the subprocessors inventory. Also want to see audit log granularity.
[02:22] Joanne: Yes, SOC2 is table stakes, but this data residency piece is the blocker. We must ensure no cross-border tokenization.

[04:01] Clara: Quick architecture overview — we have routed control where requests can be pinned by region, by account, or by API key. The control plane tags requests with tenancy and region-affinity. For EU-only, you can set region pin at the account level so requests never leave EU-backed compute.
[04:18] Martin: When you say "pin," is that enforced at the egress layer or just a routing preference?
[04:26] Clara: It's enforced — we set routing policies at the smart routing layer. If EU capacity unavailable, there are two options: fail closed or fallback to a compatible EU-hosted model variant. We don't automatically route to US unless fallback policy allows it. You can choose fail closed.
[04:44] Joanne: Fail closed is important for regs. We don't want silent fallbacks.
[05:10] Clara: Agreed. We also have tenant-level encryption keys and optional customer-managed KMS. If you supply a key (KMS), we use envelope encryption — Redwood never holds the plaintext key material in persistent storage.
[05:27] Joanne: Can you clarify "we never hold" — like HSM? And is there an escrow option?
[05:33] Clara: Good question. For KMS we integrate with cloud KMS providers (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). We support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). For added assurance we offer a KMS escrow program for enterprise where keys are held in an escrow H S M with dual control for disaster recovery — we're happy to share the whitepaper.
[06:12] Martin: Important: if keys are in our account, are you able to rotate without an outage? Our ops team needs seamless rotation.
[06:21] Clara: Yes, key rotation is supported with a grace period and versioned envelope keys. We do cross-version support in runtime so rotations don't cause service interruptions. We'll share key-rotation policy.

[08:00] Joanne: Walk me through audit logs — we need object-level logs for every request, which K user did what, and traces of model version and region.
[08:12] Clara: Audit logs include request metadata (API key, route, model id, region tag), timestamps, and response latencies. We also capture policy decisions — e.g., "failed-over-to-variant" or "blocked-fail-closed." We can stream logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[08:36] Evan: Is the log payload redacted by default, or do you capture prompts?
[08:42] Clara: By default logs contain metadata only — prompts are not stored unless you opt-in to retention for debugging. For EU-only customers we recommend prompt redact/never-store policy.

[10:05] Martin: Subprocessors — who are we talking about? Are there third-party GPU providers, monitoring agents, or analytics vendors that touch data?
[10:18] Samir: We maintain a subprocessor inventory; typical subprocessors include cloud infra providers, telemetry providers, and a managed GPU partner for burst capacity. We keep SA P L A and DPAs in place.
[10:35] Joanne: We need the list and contract language. Also want confirmation none of the subprocessors are outside the EU for EU-pinned accounts.
[10:44] Samir: Understood — Clara will pull the inventory and annotate location and data access.

[12:00] Lina: On legal side, we will need the DPA redlines and proof that subprocessors are contractually bound to not process EU data outside EU. Also need a clause for audit right.
[12:15] Clara: We can provide our standard DPA and a subprocessors map. Note some of the storage backups go to provider-managed replicated zones, but we can confine backups to EU regions when account is pinned.

[14:30] Martin: About fallback behavior again — you mentioned capable of automatically falling back to a quantized model variant; are those variants functionally identical or do they change output quality?
[14:42] Clara: Variants may be different quantization/precision levels to meet latency/cost tradeoffs; we mark variants as "compatibility tier" and evaluate them via our eval harness. Important to test your prompts.
[15:01] Joanne: So we want to test quality regressions in the pilot. We'll require acceptance criteria in rollout.

[17:20] Evan: One more on KMS — if we use our own AWS KMS in EU, does Redwood ever cache decrypted keys in memory on edge nodes?
[17:33] Clara: We avoid persistent caching. We keep in-memory only for the duration of the request, with strict TTL and hardware-backed enclaves where available. There's also a config to disable caching entirely for highest assurance.

[19:10] Samir: I want to call out the SOC2 artifacts — Penumbra asked for SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 scope, encryption whitepaper, and subprocessors map. We'll attach these to the follow-up email.
[19:25] Joanne: On ISO, is your control scope covering the control plane and data plane? We need clarity which components are in scope.
[19:34] Clara: Our ISO scope currently covers the control plane and the managed service components; we'll share the scope doc. For private/on-prem customers there's a separate attestation.

[21:00] Martin: How do you handle cross-border telemetry — is telemetry data scrubbed of PII before it leaves a region?
[21:11] Clara: Telemetry is pseudonymized; we scrub PII and can route telemetry to region-specific endpoints per account. If you require no telemetry exfiltration, we can set telemetry=none for the tenant.

[23:30] Lina: For contractual language, we will need confirmation that Redwood's subprocessors sign equivalent data processing addendums and abide by EU data transfer mechanisms (SCCs or adequacy).
[23:45] Samir: Yes, subprocessors are contracted under DPA with SCCs when necessary. We'll send the current subprocessors list and the DPA template.

[25:10] Joanne: KMS escrow — can you describe the dual-control model? Who holds the second key?
[25:20] Clara: The escrow HSM is held by a neutral third-party custodian; Redwood and customer have split access controls. Escrow is strictly for recovery and only used under defined events. We can provide the escrow contract excerpt.

[27:40] Evan: On pilot timeline — we expect to start with a small EU-only workload of 5000 requests/day. Can Redwood support that pinned to EU region?
[27:52] Clara: Yes — EU-dedicated capacity can be reserved. For pilot we'll recommend a small dedicated pool or burst capacity in EU. We'll run a short perf benchmark.

[30:30] Joanne: About identity — SSO and RBAC. We need ability to integrate with our SAML IdP and enforce SCIM provisioning, role mapping, and token expiration policies.
[30:42] Clara: We support SAML2 and OIDC SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based access controls with fine-grained permissions. We can restrict API keys to routes and models and also tie session length to your IdP policies.

[33:10] Martin: Can we get audit trail for admin actions in the console — like rollout changes, model pinning, who changed fail-closed policy?
[33:19] Clara: Yes, console admin actions are logged and exported to your audit log endpoint. Those entries show user id, action, timestamp, and previous/new value.

[35:00] Joanne: A couple of risk items — we want to ensure any third-party model evaluation data used in your quality harness doesn't contain our data.
[35:12] Clara: Absolutely — model evals are on synthetic or redacted prompts unless you give explicit permission. We'll include eval handling in the DPA appendix.

[37:40] Samir: Quick clarification on data at rest: are snapshots encrypted separately from object store encryption?
[37:48] Clara: Snapshots are encrypted with the same envelope keys. If you provide a KMS key, snapshot envelopes are encrypted under that key so object store provider can't decrypt without the KMS key.

[39:55] Lina: We'll loop legal into the DPA review. Also need to check the subcontractor list for any non-EU staffing that might access logs.
[40:07] Samir: We'll annotate who has access and the roles.

[42:30] Joanne: Last ask — can you produce a short runbook for incident response when a cross-border violation is suspected? We need steps, contacts, expected timelines.
[42:43] Clara: Yes, incident response runbook and breach notification SLA. We'll include point contacts and expected notification windows.

[44:10] Samir: Great. Recap: Samir will send SOC2/ISO artifacts; Clara will send the region-pin diagram, subprocessors list, KMS escrow brief, and key-rotation policy; Evan will share traffic profile; Lina will provide DPA redline requests; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2027-11-15.
[44:35] Joanne: Sounds good. If we get the artifacts early we'll aim to sign DPA and start pilot.
[44:50] Martin: Thanks everyone.
[45:00] Clara: One more note — I'll include a short checklist for pilot acceptance criteria (quality thresholds, latency SLO, data locality checks).
[45:10] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up with an email and links: SOC2: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/soc2, DPA template: https://redwood.example.com/legal/dpa, subprocessors: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/subprocessors.csv
[45:35] Joanne: Received, thanks.
[46:00] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hears (KMS -> K M S, HSM -> H S M), speaker overlaps at the start, and some truncated sentences.
